fields.prompt:
Create one character-proportion study for a high-definition pixel-art Three Kingdoms battlefield action game. Show exactly six Cao Wei enemy soldiers, full-body and directly front-facing, arranged in one horizontal row from left to right: 1011 heavy armored swordsman, 1012 bandit swordsman, 1013 standard bearer, 1051 archer, 1021 light shield bearer, and 1014 pottery thrower. This is a visual design comparison, not a battle scene and not a production sprite atlas.

Image 1 is the approved Enemy 1011 and controls the shared body-proportion, mass language AND the rendering style for all six: a head with substantial visual weight, broad shoulders, a compact torso and waist, short sturdy legs, substantial hands and feet, and a stable stance. All six belong to the same short, solid, serious combat-body family, with related head-to-body proportions and center of mass. The sixth soldier is the same build as the first five: the same heavy head, the same broad shoulders set high on the chest, the same compact torso and waist, the same short sturdy legs. Do not make him long, lean, lanky or narrow-shouldered. Do not make them clones with identical faces, clothing or silhouettes: heavy armor, coarse cloth, a flag, a bow, a shield and a small canteen can naturally give the six soldiers distinct equipment and poses.

First, use image 1 for the armored infantryman's established armor, helmet, red cloth and sword. He is the comparison baseline; do not redesign him as a new general.
Second, use image 2 for the bandit swordsman's visible fierce face, Han-era coarse cloth tunic, leather, limited armor, leg wraps and sword-bearing role. He also sets the rough, practical and irregular militia mood that the sixth soldier shares.
Third, use image 3 for the standard-bearer: a visible Han-era Chinese face, cloth-and-leather armor, and a two-handed grip on a long pole carrying a dark-red square military flag. No drum and no drumsticks. His body belongs to the same family as image 1; the pole and flag are not part of his body height.
Fourth, use image 4 for the archer: his narrow head cloth, cloth over the lower half of his face, wooden bow, quiver with feathered arrows and Han-era cloth-and-leather military kit. His body belongs to the same family as image 1, while his equipment remains lighter than the armored infantryman's.
Fifth, use image 5 for the light shield bearer: keep all of his equipment, stance and identity, including the broad rectangular timber shield with dark iron bands and studs, held upright in front of his body on the LEFT side of the picture, in front of his right arm, with his right arm hidden behind it and his left arm hanging free at his side. This is already correct in image 5: keep the shield exactly where it is, on the LEFT side of the picture. Do not mirror him and do not swap arms. His plain dark cloth cap, cross-collar grey-beige cloth tunic, small dark armor plates, leather belt, bracers, dark trousers, pale leg wraps and heavy boots all stay as they are.

Sixth and last is the Cao Wei pottery thrower, and he is the point of this study. Image 6 is his approved design and face, and the body build of the first five soldiers is his body build as well. He is a low-ranking militia man from the same rough, bandit-like background as the second soldier: practical, poorly equipped, irregular, not a regular army soldier. His face is exposed, with lowered brows and a sly, cunning, almost amused expression; his eyes narrow into short slits, the outer ends of his eyebrows lift while the inner ends press down, and his mouth opens into a crooked toothy grin with one corner of the mouth pulled higher than the other, so the expression is lopsided. Short dark stubble covers his jaw and cheeks. His face is lean and sharp rather than broad: the cheeks drawn in, an angular cheekbone line, a jaw that tapers to a slightly pointed chin, a narrow forehead and a slim nose bridge.
His clothing is worn, coarse and improvised: a grey-beige or dark brown crossed-collar coarse cloth tunic, a dark brown leather shoulder strap, a belt with a small cloth pouch, dark trousers, pale leg wraps and worn cloth shoes. His kit is light and uneven, with no body armor of any kind.
He carries no sword, knife, spear, bow, quiver, flag or shield. His only combat prop is one ordinary personal ceramic water canteen, the kind a militia man carries for drinking: a slightly flattened round body, a short neck, a small spout and one small handle or carrying cord. It is small enough to hold in one hand, roughly one eighth to one tenth of his body height. Plain warm brown or gray-brown unglazed pottery, with no pattern, no glaze, no gold trim and no glow.
For the identity pose he stands facing forward with both feet planted, and his face looks straight out of the picture at the viewer. The canteen hangs at the LEFT side of the picture, at his right waist, or rests naturally in his right hand; the other hand hangs naturally or helps balance. He presents the canteen at rest, not in a throwing motion. His face, both hands, the canteen and both feet are fully visible.

RENDERING STYLE MUST MATCH: image 1 supplies the rendering style for all six, not just the body proportions. Draw every soldier in exactly the same rendering — the same chunky clustered pixel planes, the same hard-edged colour clusters, the same stepped silhouettes, the same outline weight, the same lighting and the same level of detail. Each soldier's face, cloth and leather are built from the same number of colour clusters as the armored infantryman. Nobody is smoother, airbrushed, glossier, more painterly or more finely detailed than the others. All six must look like they come out of the same game.

Place the six pairs of feet on a shared visual baseline and make their body heights broadly comparable. The sixth soldier's body height should be about 0.94 to 0.99 of the armored infantryman's body height. Do not count the plume, flagpole, flag, sword, bow, quiver, shield or canteen as body height. Leave visible space between figures so every head, shoulder, torso, pair of hands and pair of feet can be judged separately; the flag, the weapons, the shield and the canteen must not cover another soldier. All six face the player directly and all six look straight out of the picture at the viewer. Do not use perspective depth to make one soldier larger or smaller, and do not stretch or shrink an entire body to disguise incorrect internal proportions.

Use high-definition pixel-art Three Kingdoms action-game rendering: clean dark contours, clustered light and shadow planes, solid cool iron and warm cloth / leather volumes. Compact and fierce, not cute. Landscape composition, one single flat uniform neutral grey background with no vignette and no glow around the figures, only the six characters. No environment, no ground plane, no perspective floor, no battle effects, no interface, no text, no labels, no numbers, no watermark and no checkerboard.

Negative constraints: seven characters, fewer than six characters, duplicated character, missing character, wrong order, side view, three-quarter view, turned body, looking away, looking sideways, cross-eyed, inconsistent baseline, perspective depth, oversized 1014, tiny 1014, lanky 1014, narrow shoulders on 1014, long legs on 1014, elongated body, stretched body, cropped feet, cropped head, extra limb, hidden face, missing hands, missing feet, prop overlapping neighboring character, weapon overlap, mirrored character, identical clone faces, identical armor on all characters, long-legged realistic anatomy, tiny heads, extreme toy-like chibi, giant boss, 1014 wearing helmet, 1014 wearing wide-brimmed hat, 1014 wearing face mask, 1014 wearing full body armor, 1014 with plated shoulder armor, 1014 with oversized bracers, 1014 as a mage, 1014 as a pot maker, 1014 as a noble officer, 1014 as a general, 1014 as an elite regular soldier, large jar, wine jar, wine barrel, large amphora, oversized pottery, heavy ceramic vessel, two-handed jar hug, carrying a large container, bottle covering torso, bottle larger than one hand, magic bottle, green glowing poison, glowing bottle, grenade-shaped bottle, modern grenade, modern military uniform, sword, knife, spear, bow, quiver, flag, flagpole, shield, gold trim, glazed pottery, painted ceramic pattern, runes, vase, gourd, bomb, smooth rendering, glossy highlights, painterly rendering, soft gradients, airbrushed shading, finer detail on one character, photorealism, 3D render, glossy 3D plastic, western fantasy knight, anime moe, watercolor, blur, random pixel noise, gray halo, white halo, ground shadow, scenery, ground plane, battle effects, spell circle, text, labels, numbers, logo, watermark, UI, checkerboard
